analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: A strong US CPI print followed by mounting AI-trade fears produced a very volatile session. The S&P 500 fell -1.11%, its worst day since July, and futures were down another -0.50% this morning.
The 10yr Treasury yield surged to 5.33% after CPI, closed at 5.19%, and is down another -8.4bps to 5.10% this morning. The intraday range was very large.
Asia sold off sharply overnight. The KOSPI fell -7.04% (a circuit breaker triggered) and the Nikkei fell -5.08%. SK Hynix fell -11.28% and Samsung fell -9.91%.

AI-linked credit stress is spreading. CoreWeave 5yr CDS rose +136bps to 1118bps after crossing 1000bps intraday Tuesday, and its shares fell -15.46%. Oracle fell -8.83%, its largest decline since June.
The Philly semiconductor index fell -4.30% for a 6th consecutive decline, the first such streak in over a year. It is down -11.6% over the 6 sessions.

September CPI was hot. Headline was +0.649% on the month (vs +0.6% expected) and +3.7% on the year. Core was +0.335% on the month (vs +0.2% expected) and +2.6% on the year (vs +2.5% expected). The report says price pressure was broad-based across the consumer basket, not just energy.

Market pricing for an October Fed hike rose from 22% before CPI to an intraday peak of 58%, and spent about half an hour above 50%. It has since unwound to 27% this morning as AI and credit fears outweighed the print.
US HY spreads widened +11bps to 324bps, the widest since March. The report links the fall in hike odds to fears of tighter credit conditions.
The Russell 2000 fell -1.93% and entered correction territory, down over -10% from its August peak.
The 2yr yield was up +16.1bps intraday, closed +0.8bps at 4.80%, and is down -7.8bps to 4.72% this morning. The 30yr peaked at 5.63%, closed at 5.52% and is at 5.45% this morning.
The initial dollar rally after CPI has fully reversed. EUR/USD is up +0.53% this morning to $1.1215.
Brent closed +0.35% at $106.06/bbl amid no progress in the US-Iran conflict. It is down -1.75% to $104.20 overnight despite Zelenskyy saying Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian refineries.

European assets outperformed. The STOXX 600 rose +0.43% to a two-week high, but the Franco-German 10yr spread widened +4.1bps to 141.5bps, near Monday's closing peak of 142.3bps. DAX futures are down -0.49% today.

Today's calendar has US PPI and retail sales for September, Empire State survey, jobless claims, UK GDP and Euro Area industrial production. Fed speakers are Goolsbee and Hammack, BoE speakers are Greene and Breeden, and EU leaders meet in Brussels.

market_movers.rationale: 5yr CDS rose to 1118bps from above 1000bps intraday Tuesday, and shares fell -15.46%. Credit investors are worried about its leverage profile.
Shares fell -8.83%, the largest decline since June, as credit scrutiny of heavy-capex AI firms spread.

sector_views.rationale: The Philly semiconductor index fell 6 straight sessions, down -11.6% in total. SK Hynix and Samsung fell about -11% and -10% in Asia.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Just short of rounding up to +0.7%. It fed speculation about an October Fed hike.
Energy prices drove much of the rise.
The surprise was broad-based across the consumer basket, not just energy.
Core ran above consensus on the year.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The post-CPI spike has unwound as AI and credit fears dominate.

risk_factors: AI-linked credit stress from heavy capex and leverage could tighten broader credit conditions.
A hot CPI raises the risk of Fed tightening, with an October hike priced at 27%.
Oil near $104-106 with the US-Iran conflict unresolved adds to inflation pressure.
Widening French-German sovereign spreads in Europe, at 141.5bps.
Contagion from the Asia selloff to US and European equities, with NASDAQ 100 futures down -1.08%.
vol_and_positioning: CDX HY was 106.14 (-0.433 pts), and US HY spreads were 324bps, the widest since March.
The 5yr CoreWeave CDS closed at 1118bps. The Philly semiconductor index fell 6 sessions in a row, the first such streak in over a year.
geopolitical: No signs of progress in the US-Iran conflict, which added to oil and inflation concerns.
Ukrainian President Zelenskyy told the FT that Ukraine would resume strikes on Russian refineries.
EU leaders meet for a summit in Brussels.

tension_points.theme: hot CPI vs AI credit stress
tension_points.bull_case: A strong CPI print (core +0.335% m/m) raised the odds of an October Fed hike to as much as 58% intraday.
tension_points.bear_case: AI-linked credit stress and risk-off pushed hike odds back to 27%. Fears of broader credit tightening cast doubt that the Fed would act despite the print.
